english:
The Lord has created this world of living beings as a plaything, along with its bodies, for the sake of love and affection. The rule of this play is that the objects of the play are meant only for the sake of playing and not for personal use. However, this world of living beings has forgotten the play and has started considering the objects of the play, i.e., the bodies, as personal. This has led to its entanglement and complete separation from the Lord.

The play was not played alone by the Lord (Ekaki, 18th verse of the 18th chapter), nor was it played by Brahma when he appeared and disappeared (new 7th and 8th verses of the 11th chapter), nor is it played by the living beings in the present time by being under the control of nature (5th verse of the 3rd chapter). The living being is bound to be born and die, and to perform actions and enjoy their fruits - it will never be free from this calamity. This proves that as long as the realization of the Supreme Being does not take place, and it does not give up its relationship with nature, it cannot escape the cycle of birth and death due to its bondage.

However, when its nature and the nature-born objects cease to control it, i.e., when it realizes its pure form, it is not born in the creation and is not affected in the destruction - 'sarge'api nopajayante pralaye na vyathanti cha' (Gita 14.2).

The words 'bhutva bhutva praliyate' are said for the bodies, which are constantly being born and destroyed, i.e., which are constantly undergoing change. However, the living being considers the change in the bodies as its own change and its own birth and death. This is the reason why it is called birth and death.

This is the very essence of the Self - 'bhutagraham sa evayam' and the bodies are transitory - 'bhutva bhutva praliyate'. Therefore, holding onto the bodies, i.e., undergoing birth and death, is a lower duty, and liberation is a higher duty.

In the original, the bondage is due to the control of nature-born objects, considering them as important, and accepting them - 'ratriyagame' avashah parth prabhavatyaharagame'. Here, 'avashah' means that if the living being remains under the control of nature, i.e., if it considers any object as its own, as long as it desires to enjoy the pleasure of the objects, it will be under the illusion that 'I am the owner of this object. I am under the control of this object due to the desire for the pleasure of the objects'. It will be under the control of the objects and will be a slave. It will be enjoying the objects and will be under the illusion that the more it accepts the objects, the more it will be free from bondage, but it will be difficult to give up the objects. It will become a great slave. However, this bondage is created by itself, not by itself, and it will never be free from bondage. Brahma's creation and destruction are going on. Therefore, it is its responsibility to give up this bondage. It can give up this bondage whenever it wants.

Supplementary note - The world is a changing department, and the changeless department is the conscious existence. The one that has been in the flow of birth and death since time immemorial is the living being-community, which is constantly being born and destroyed. The living being is constantly being born and dying between Brahma's day and night. The meaning is that the one that is constantly being born and destroyed is the world, and the one that remains the same (the one that was in the creation stage) is the true form of the living being, which is the conscious existence, the very essence of the Supreme Being. The conscious existence is the power of self-acceptance or self-rejection. Due to the misuse of this power, i.e., due to the acceptance of ignorance, the living being is born and dies - 'karanam gunasango'sya sad-asad-yoni-janmasu' (Gita 13.21). If it does not misuse this power, its birth and death cannot take place. Therefore, the special goal of the living being is to not accept ignorance, i.e., to remain in its true form or to take refuge in the Lord, its part. Ignorance is the acceptance of change, i.e., the acceptance of the change in the country, time, object, person, action, state, and circumstances, but there is no change in the self - this is the experience of a human being. However, despite this experience, a human being remains bound to pleasure due to attachment and remains bound to ignorance, from which it cannot be freed.
